# Norman Douglas

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male
- **Status:** Alive
- **Origin:** Glen St. Mary
- **Role:** Farmer

## Appearance

Norman Douglas is an elderly farmer with a loud voice and a rugged, weathered appearance. He has a broad, burly build and an intimidating presence that often frightens those who do not know him well.

## Personality

He is famously gruff, blunt, and hot-tempered, often speaking in a booming voice and engaging in fierce arguments. Despite his fiery outward demeanor and profane reputation, he possesses a deeply soft heart and genuine loyalty to his friends. He holds strong political convictions and takes great pride in his independence.

## Traits

- Blunt and outspoken
- Hot-tempered
- Kind-hearted beneath a rough exterior
- Opinionated

## Abilities

- Farming

## Goals

- To live on his own terms and support those he cares about despite his abrasive nature

## History

Norman Douglas is a well-known figure in Glen St. Mary, famous for his loud arguments and uncompromising personality. For many years, he engaged in a prolonged engagement and frequent quarrels with Ellen West. During a severe illness, he repents his blustering ways, though he quickly returns to his usual fiery self upon recovering. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe settle at the House of Dreams, Norman interacts with their circle, including Miss Cornelia Bryant, with whom he frequently clashes over politics and religion. Eventually, after decades of misunderstanding and stubbornness, he finally marries Ellen West.

## Background by volume

- Longtime resident and farmer in the Glen St. Mary community
- Had a long-standing, tempestuous courtship with Ellen West

## Relationships

### Ellen West

- Spouse of — Married after a decades-long courtship and frequent arguments

- Rival of — Frequent political and personal antagonist who later comes to respect him
